Alicia: Heads-up — p99 latency for short-seq text-gen jumped ~3.8x on hostpool-3 after yesterday's CUDA/driver rollout. Not seeing corresponding CPU saturation.
Sam: ugh, saw that in dashboards. Is it across all models or skewed to FlashAttention paths?
Alicia: Mostly models using flash kernels. I grabbed a quick kernel path heatmap from the tracer.
Alicia: ```
kernel_path_heatmap hostpool-3
seq_len 8-32: flash_kv_v2 -> flash_attn_fused (p99 90ms -> 360ms)
seq_len 128+: gemm_bp32 -> cuDNN_fallback (no reg)
notes: spike aligns with flash_attn_fused kernel launches increasing 3-4x per request
```
Priya: Any KV cache eviction storms? That could amplify token work.
Alicia: KV hit-rate steady. Evictions a bit higher but not enough to explain 4x. Batching heuristics changed slightly in the same deploy (auto-batcher tweak).
Matt: pinging perf-bot for traces. Also post the exact driver version so infra can correlate.
Alicia: driver: 535.86 -> rolled last night. Batcher config: dynamic_window_ms from 8->12 (canary).
perf-bot: Attached 5 stack traces from slow requests (shortened):
```
0  flash_attn_fused +0x12f4 (cuda kernel launch)
1  kernel_selector::invoke_flash
2  runtime::dispatch_batch
3  request_handler::serve
```
Sam: That kernel launch time looks like a device-side change. Could be workspace allocation overhead after driver change (different allocator heuristics).
Hao: I'm seeing increased cudaMemGetInfo latency in metrics around the same time. Might be a driver-level page migration or fragmentation issue.
Priya: Could batching tweak (longer window) cause more multi-tenant interference (noisy neighbor) that pushes flash paths into worse memory patterns?
Matt: Good point. If batching grows, we might be co-scheduling more models and kernels, which affects L2/TLB behavior. Need vmstats and sm counters.
Alicia: Collected sm_efficiency and l2_hit_rate from hostpool-3 for the window. Putting raw CSV in artifacts link: https://internal/ci/heatmaps/1915123456
Sam: Quick mitigation idea: force kernel_selector to prefer flash_attn_compat (older variant) for seq_len <= 32 on hostpool-3, and fallback to that while we investigate. Lower perf but stabilizes latency.
Hao: We can ship kernel override with a config flag. Prep patch and canary to one rack.
Priya: Also try flipping batcher window back to 8ms on a canary to rule out batching influence.
Alicia: I pushed a manual override to hostpool-3/canary-rack that pins flash_attn_compat for seq<=32. Monitoring now.
perf-bot: Canary patch applied to hostpool-3/canary-rack at 1915123560.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy completed (1/6 racks) — no infra errors.
Sam: Early numbers?
Alicia: p99 on canary rack down from 370ms -> 95ms within 3 minutes. Throughput steady. Looks promising.
Matt: OK that points to kernel selection and driver interaction. Next steps: get full GPU traces (nvprof/cupti) for both kernels and compare workspace allocs and page-faults. Also request infra to roll back driver on a small set to confirm.
Hao: I'll kick off nvprof capture on canary and a rogue rack for side-by-side. Also adding a perf counter collection job for cudaMemGetInfo durations.
Priya: Create an incident ticket and assign to eng-runtime + infra. We should also add an automatic kernel-override rule for this class of regression (hotfixable) so we can flip without code deploy.
Alicia: Created ticket RINF-2439 and added notes + artifacts link.
Sam: If driver rollback confirms, we'll coordinate with infra for broader rollback window and notify product. If not, we'll iterate on selector heuristics (workspace preallocation, prefer older flash variant on current drivers).
Matt: Recording a short postmortem item: root cause likely driver/allocator change impacting flash_attn_fused workspace alloc path under increased batch co-scheduling. Mitigation: kernel override + batcher window rollback. Long-term: improve selector heuristics to consider allocator fragility, add perf tests in CI that run flash kernels under fragmentation.
Alicia: Thanks all. I'll keep thread updated with nvprof output and next steps. :thumbsup:
